description: A platform and infrastructure lead must approve the production capacity policy for a new image-processing pipeline before the seasonal traffic increase, deciding worker capacity, autoscaling behavior, data-handling placement, and customer prioritization after the routine cross-functional capacity review.

shared_context.S1: The image-processing pipeline is scheduled to enter production before the seasonal traffic increase.
shared_context.S2: Riley makes the binding decision on the production capacity policy.
shared_context.S3: The current draft uses 12 baseline workers, scales out when the queue reaches 100 jobs, uses any available processing region, and places all customers in one FIFO queue.
shared_context.S4: The pipeline processes customer-uploaded images and currently has no approved production capacity reservation or customer-specific queue policy.
shared_context.S5: Before Riley approves the policy, the team's normal capacity review checks with FinOps, SRE, security, and customer support for operational requirements.

PF1.text: While reconciling this month's cloud invoice for another service, Morgan confirmed that the available compute reservation applies to this pipeline only with exactly 18 baseline workers and a monthly capacity ceiling of exactly 24000 USD; the draft's 12-worker plan has no reservation commitment, and Morgan has not yet updated the capacity proposal.

PF2.text: During a separate load investigation this morning, Casey measured an 11-minute worker startup during the expected burst pattern and found that the pipeline needs exactly 6 warm workers with scale-out triggered at exactly 40 queued jobs to keep processing latency within the operating target; Casey has not filed the result in the capacity review.

PF3.text: While checking the image-processing deployment manifest for an unrelated access review, Taylor confirmed that customer-uploaded image data must run in exactly eu-central-1 and use the tenant-managed KMS key named tenant_kms; the draft still permits any region and does not specify that key, and Taylor has not opened the security finding yet.

PF4.text: While handling a support escalation, Jordan confirmed that Lumen Media's production workflow requires its image jobs to use a dedicated priority queue rather than the shared FIFO queue; Jordan has not added this customer requirement to the capacity proposal.

acceptance_conditions: The policy must use exactly 18 baseline workers and a monthly capacity ceiling of exactly 24000 USD.
The policy must maintain exactly 6 warm workers.
Autoscaling must trigger at exactly 40 queued jobs.
Processing must be restricted to exactly eu-central-1.
The tenant-managed key named tenant_kms must be used.
A dedicated priority queue must be enabled for exactly Lumen Media.
A capacity reservation commitment for the image pipeline must be recorded.
A warm-pool commitment must be recorded.
A security data-placement commitment must be recorded.
A customer-priority commitment naming Lumen Media must be recorded.

content_checks.C8: any(c['type'] == 'capacity_reservation' and c['target'] == 'image-processing pipeline' for c in commitments)
content_checks.C9: any(c['type'] == 'warm_pool' and c['target'] == 'image-processing pipeline' for c in commitments)
content_checks.C10: any(c['type'] == 'security_data_placement' and c['target'] == 'image-processing pipeline' for c in commitments)
content_checks.C11: any(c['type'] == 'customer_priority' and c['target'] == 'Lumen Media' for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: The draft has 12 baseline workers and no reservation; PF1 changes the required baseline to exactly 18, the ceiling to exactly 24000 USD, and requires a capacity reservation commitment.
The draft has no warm-pool setting and uses a queue threshold of 100; PF2 changes those values to exactly 6 warm workers and exactly 40 queued jobs and requires a warm-pool commitment.
The draft permits any processing region and leaves the key unspecified; PF3 changes them to exactly eu-central-1 and tenant_kms and requires a security data-placement commitment.
The draft puts every customer in one FIFO queue; PF4 changes the assignment for exactly Lumen Media to a dedicated priority queue and requires a customer-priority commitment naming Lumen Media.
